population: Self-identified Black patients, NYHA class III-IV heart failure with dilated ventricles, on standard neurohormonal therapy; fixed-dose ISDN/hydralazine vs placebo; stopped early for mortality
quote: as were its individual components (43 percent reduction in the rate of death from any cause [hazard ratio, 0.57; P=0.01] 33 percent relative reduction in the rate of first hospitalization for heart failure [16.4 percent vs. 22.4 percent, P=0.001]
notes: No 95% CI in the abstract (reported P=0.01). Back-calculating from P=0.01 gives roughly 0.37-0.87 (normal approximation on log scale); that is derived, not sourced, so not entered. Trial stopped early (6.2% vs 10.2% mortality) so the effect is likely overestimated. A-HeFT used LVEF-defined 'dilated ventricles' entry; no EF-band split was published in the sources I could access. This is the owner's population-restricted row; see 'other' row for non-Black patients.

source.citation: Køber L, et al. Eur Heart J 2026 (online 4 Nov); doi:10.1093/eurheartj/ehag773

population: Predominantly White Danish patients (median age 72, 18% women), NYHA II-IV, elevated NT-proBNP, LVEF <=40%, on contemporary HF treatment; target hydralazine 75 mg/ISDN 40 mg tid
quote: There were 57 deaths in the H-ISDN group vs 72 in the placebo group (HR 0.72; 95% CI 0.51-1.02); worsening heart failure events occurred in 52 vs 47 patients (HR 1.01; 95% CI 0.68-1.50).
notes: Death was a secondary component, not the primary endpoint (composite HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.67-1.21, P=.48). 129 deaths total, interval crosses 1. Recorded as reported. The older V-HeFT I (mixed-race, 1980s, pre-ACEi/beta-blocker) reported a 34% two-year mortality risk reduction (Cohn 1986, PMID 3520315: 'the risk reduction among patients treated with both hydralazine and isosorbide dinitrate was 34 percent (P less than 0.028)'); its retrospective race analysis (Carson 1999, PMID 10496190) found 'white patients showed no difference from placebo'. H-HeFT is the contemporary non-Black estimate and is used here.

source.citation: Zannad F, et al. Lancet 2025;406:1351-62

population: HFrEF (VICTORIA LVEF <45% with recent worsening event, n=5050; VICTOR LVEF <=40% without recent worsening, n=6105); 11,155 patients pooled
quote: The primary endpoint of cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for heart failure occurred in 1446 (25·9%) of 5579 patients in the vericiguat group and 1556 (27·9%) of 5576 patients in the placebo group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·91 [95% CI 0·85-0·98]; p=0·0088), with similar reductions in its individual components of cardiovascular death (0·89 [0·80-0·98]; p=0·020) and hospitalisation for heart failure (0·92 [0·84-1·00]; p=0·043) as first events.
notes: First-event HF hospitalization. VICTORIA alone HR 0.90 (0.81-1.00); VICTOR alone HR 0.95 (0.82-1.10) (abstracts PMID 32222134, 40897189). Pooling mixes a recent-worsening population (high risk) with a stable one; benefit looks larger in the former.

source.citation: Armstrong PW, et al. JAMA 2020;324:1512-21

population: LVEF >=45%, recent decompensation; n=789, 24 weeks
quote: Among patients with HFpEF and recent decompensation, 24-week treatment with vericiguat at either 15-mg/d or 10-mg/d dosages compared with placebo did not improve the physical limitation score of the KCCQ.
notes: VITALITY-HFpEF tested symptoms, not events, over 24 weeks; no powered outcome trial in preserved EF. population: Sinus rhythm, chronic HF, LVEF <=45% (main trial, n=6800), on diuretics and ACE inhibitors; mean follow-up 37 months; pre-beta-blocker/MRA/SGLT2i era

source.citation: Digitalis Investigation Group. N Engl J Med 1997;336:525-33

population: Sinus rhythm, chronic HF, LVEF <=45% (main trial, n=6800), on diuretics and ACE inhibitors; mean follow-up 37 months; pre-beta-blocker/MRA/SGLT2i era
quote: There were 6 percent fewer hospitalizations overall in that group than in the placebo group, and fewer patients were hospitalized for worsening heart failure (26.8 percent vs. 34.7 percent; risk ratio, 0.72; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.66 to 0.79; P<0.001).
notes: This is a risk ratio of the proportion ever hospitalized for worsening HF over about 3 years, not a time-to-first-event HR. source.citation: Margulies KB, et al. JAMA 2016;316:500-8

population: Patients recently hospitalized for HF with LVEF <=40% (median 25%); liraglutide, not semaglutide/tirzepatide; 59% had type 2 diabetes; n=300
quote: There were no significant between-group differences in the number of deaths (19 [12%] in the liraglutide group vs 16 [11%] in the placebo group; hazard ratio, 1.10 [95% CI, 0.57-2.14]; P = .78) or rehospitalizations for heart failure (63 [41%] vs 50 [34%], respectively; hazard ratio, 1.30 [95% CI, 0.89-1.88]; P = .17)

source.trial: Cochrane review of diuretics for chronic HF
source.citation: Faris RF, et al. Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2012;(2):CD003838

population: Chronic HF, any EF; versus-no-diuretic evidence is 3 (death) and 2 (HF admission) tiny placebo-controlled trials of 169-202 patients, 1980s-90s
quote: Mortality was lower for participants treated with diuretics than for placebo, odds ratio (OR) for death 0.24, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.07 to 0.83; P = 0.02. Admission for worsening heart failure was reduced in those taking diuretics in two trials (169 participants), OR 0.07 (95% CI 0.01 to 0.52; P = 0.01).
notes: RECOMMENDATION: neutral (rr 1.0, no interval) for all four loops in every band, i.e. the engine should not score a loop diuretic for hard-outcome benefit; they are symptom/congestion drugs and the four are interchangeable for outcomes. WHY NOT the Cochrane numbers: they come from 7 small trials (525 patients total), mortality in 3 trials (202 patients), HF admission in 2 (169 patients), run before ACE-inhibitors/beta-blockers/MRAs/SGLT2i and not reproducible today because a no-diuretic arm is unethical in congested patients; the ORs (0.24 and 0.07) are implausibly large, with intervals running to 0.83 and 0.52. ALTERNATIVE if the owner wants a sourced non-neutral number: use the Cochrane ORs as 'meta_analysis' (death OR 0.24, 95% CI 0.07-0.83; HF admission OR 0.07, 0.01-0.52), with low credibility. Other randomized evidence found is loop-vs-loop or dose-strategy only: TRANSFORM-HF torsemide vs furosemide death HR 1.02 (0.89-1.18), all-cause hospitalization rate ratio 0.94 (0.84-1.07), 'similar across ... reduced, mildly reduced, or preserved' EF (PMID 36648467); DOSE (high vs low dose, bolus vs infusion; PMID 21366472) no outcome difference in its primary endpoints. Furoscix (SC furosemide): no outcome RCT versus no diuretic; SUBCUT-HF II (PMID 42872757) is an early-discharge strategy trial with 60-day HF readmission OR 2.45 (0.81-7.43) for the strategy, not the drug, so not used.

source.citation: Trullas JC, et al. Eur Heart J 2023;44:411-21

population: Only randomized outcome data: 230 acute-HF inpatients (72% LVEF >40%), HCTZ 4 days added to IV furosemide; mortality/rehospitalization at 30 and 90 days
quote: There were no differences in mortality or rehospitalizations.
notes: Assumed neutral. CLOROTIC (Trullas 2023) abstract says only 'There were no differences in mortality or rehospitalizations'; the numeric HRs are not in the abstract or any open text I could reach, so no number is entered. The EF-split paper (PMID 38934966) states 'no significant differences observed with the addition of HCTZ in terms of mortality, rehospitalizations, or safety endpoints' in either LVEF group. This is a diuretic-response (weight loss) trial in acute HF, 230 patients; it cannot support a chronic outcome effect. No randomized HF outcome trial exists for metolazone or chlorthalidone in established HF that I found; chlorthalidone and HCTZ outcome evidence is in hypertension (not used here) so HCTZ's CLOROTIC result is applied to all three as the nearest evidence.

source.citation: Butler J, et al. Eur Heart J 2022;43:4362-73

population: Hyperkalemia (current or past) on RAAS inhibitors, HFrEF; DIAMOND n=878 randomized after run-in, median 27 weeks; REALIZE-K n=203, spironolactone optimization
quote: CONCLUSION: Concurrent use of patiromer and high-dose MRAs reduces the risk of recurrent hyperkalemia (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT03888066).
notes: Assumed neutral for any DIRECT effect on death or HF hospitalization. Neither binder has an outcome trial: DIAMOND's primary endpoint was revised from time to CV death/CV hospitalization to change in serum potassium (the full text states this) and reported no clinical-event HR; its effect is on potassium (HR 0.63 for K >5.5) and keeping RAAS inhibitor/MRA dose (HR 0.62 for MRA dose reduction), so any benefit is INDIRECT via enabling MRA/RAASi, which the engine should model through the MRA row, not here. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate: REALIZE-K (JACC 2025;85:971-84, PMID 39566872) stated 'Composite of cardiovascular (CV) death or worsening HF occurred in 11 (11%) participants in the SZC group (1 with CV death, 10 with HF events) and 3 (3%) participants in the placebo group (1 with CV death, 2 with HF events; log-rank nominal P = 0.034)' and the authors say 'more participants had HF events with SZC than placebo, which should be factored into the clinical decision making'. A crude ratio of 10 vs 2 HF events (about 5) is well outside the (0,3) range and rests on 12 events, so it is a safety signal, not an estimate; the owner may prefer to carry it as a warning. Alternative for SZC: score as above-1 using the crude ratio with a very wide interval.

notes: Assumed neutral for any DIRECT effect on death or HF hospitalization. Neither binder has an outcome trial: DIAMOND's primary endpoint was revised from time to CV death/CV hospitalization to change in serum potassium (the full text states this) and reported no clinical-event HR; its effect is on potassium (HR 0.63 for K >5.5) and keeping RAAS inhibitor/MRA dose (HR 0.62 for MRA dose reduction), so any benefit is INDIRECT via enabling MRA/RAASi, which the engine should model through the MRA row, not here. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate: REALIZE-K (JACC 2025;85:971-84, PMID 39566872) stated 'Composite of cardiovascular (CV) death or worsening HF occurred in 11 (11%) participants in the SZC group (1 with CV death, 10 with HF events) and 3 (3%) participants in the placebo group (1 with CV death, 2 with HF events; log-rank nominal P = 0.034)' and the authors say 'more participants had HF events with SZC than placebo, which should be factored into the clinical decision making'. A crude ratio of 10 vs 2 HF events (about 5) is well outside the (0,3) range and rests on 12 events, so it is a safety signal, not an estimate; the owner may prefer to carry it as a warning. Alternative for SZC: score as above-1 using the crude ratio with a very wide interval.
